title: Service threshold exceedance and fallback playbook alignment
summary: Bridge call to align on the May 12th threshold-exceeding incident. Reviewed timeline, identified primary contributing factors (KV cache coldstarts + burst pattern from nightly ETL), agreed on short-term mitigations (targeted warmup, transient prefilling, adjust autoscale threshold for model variant fallback) and longer-term reliability improvements (canary policy, better telemetry for longtail errors, runbook updates). Decided owners and dates for pilot and follow-ups.
next_steps: Redwood to share incident timeline + detailed memos and logs (link) by 2026-05-20
Cascade SRE to run KV cache warmup and prefilling test and share results by 2026-05-22
SE-run benchmark of fallback policy with reduced model variant and report latency/cost tradeoffs by 2026-05-25
Schedule 30-min canary rollout planning session w/ engineering on 2026-05-27
action_items: Sofia Alvarez - run KV cache warmup/prefill test against prod-like load and upload results to shared sheet - due 2026-05-22
Ethan Cho - produce fallback policy sim (policy.yaml + expected token cost delta) and attach latency histogram - due 2026-05-25
Maya Patel - share full incident logs and the Redwood post-incident memo (redwood.in/incident/CH-472) - due 2026-05-20
Tom Becker - confirm stakeholder list for canary (prod owners + compliance) and send invites - due 2026-05-21
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-18
Start: 14:30 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cho (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Ravi Menon (Cascade CTO), Sofia Alvarez (Cascade SRE), Tom Becker (Cascade PM)

Auto-summary (system): Short call to align on the May 12th availability spike, agree mitigations and owners.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to go over the threshold exceedance you saw last week and make sure the short term fixes and the rollout plan are clear. Ravi, you okay to start with a quick recap?

[00:22] Ravi (Cascade): Yeah, sure. Um, thanks. So on May 12th we saw a — like a steep increase in tail latency starting around 03:15 UTC, about 40 minutes, and it led to a cascade where several routes hit concurrency limits. We cut traffic manually to the dedicated pool and that helped, but the main pain point was the model KV cache being cold after the nightly ETL fan-out and the autoscaler not triggering fallback fast enough.

[00:51] Sofia (Cascade): Sorry interject, yeah the coldstart is the big one. We have that batch ETL that refreshes user embeddings, which results in many prefix misses. The prefill didn't kick in because our warmup job is only scheduled at 02:00 and didn't cover the new prefixes.

[01:10] Ethan (Redwood SE): Right, so from our side the runtime saw a sudden spike in KV cache misses and the continuous batching queue grew. We have heuristics to spill to async queue but when the miss rate + concurrency both spike we throttle downstream which in your case hit the route-level SLOs. Also we saw a couple of QP (quantization parameter) fallbacks — the model variant switch added extra overhead in the hot path.

[01:42] Tom (Cascade): The timeline you guys shared earlier — is there a link to the raw logs? I want to correlate with our job scheduler traces.

[01:50] Maya (Redwood): Yes, we'll share the incident bundle — redwood.in/incident/CH-472 — full logs and a short memo. We'll add the exact timestamps and the key metrics.

[02:05] Lena (Redwood CSM): Quick note — from a customer ops perspective, we want to make sure the fallback behavior is deterministic and documented in the runbook. Last time the fallback kicked in at different thresholds for different model variants which confused your on-call.

[02:25] Sofia (Cascade): Yeah, we had mixed signals. One service was falling back to the optimized-8bit variant, another to a smaller architecture, and the latency/cost impacts were inconsistent.

[02:45] Ethan (Redwood SE): That's on us to make policy consistent. We can provide a 'single' fallback policy template: prefer smaller architecture first, then optimized quantized variant as the second line, and finally route-level queue shedding. The key is predictable SLOs during the degrade mode.

[03:12] Ravi (Cascade): Can that policy be simulated? We need to show execs the expected end-to-end latency and cost impact.

[03:22] Ethan (Redwood SE): Absolutely. I'll run a simulation using your request traces — that's the plan after this call. We'll produce a histogram of p50/p95/p99 and token cost delta.

[03:40] Tom (Cascade): Also curious about why the autoscaler didn't act sooner. We expected scale-out at 55% GPU util but we saw the system hang with 80% queue depth.

[03:51] Maya (Redwood): Two things: first, scale triggers are hybrid (util + queue depth) and there's a cooldown window to avoid thrash. Second, because the workload pattern was a rapid simultaneous fan-out we actually recommend a pre-burst policy (scheduled scale-up) for ETL windows.

[04:13] Sofia (Cascade): A scheduled pre-burst would have helped, yeah. But ops drifted the ETL timing a bit; doesn't always run at the same minute. Can Redwood support a short window with conservative scheduled capacity that automatically retracts?

[04:28] Ethan (Redwood SE): Yes, Redwood Dedicated supports scheduled capacity windows and burst pools. We can propose a conservative buffer — say +15% capacity for a 30-minute window around your bulk job, and a warmup prefill job to prime the KV cache. That minimizes the reliance on autoscaler reaction time.

[04:52] Ravi (Cascade): Sounds good. Is there cost-estimate for that buffer? CFO will ask.

[05:00] Maya (Redwood): We'll include cost delta in the follow-up doc. It depends on committed vs burst billing; we'll show expected token/GPU hour impact for a sample week.

[05:15] Tom (Cascade): On security: there's a note from our compliance team about audit logs and KMS usage during failover. We need to make sure the fallback doesn't change key access patterns or write logs to a different bucket.

[05:28] Lena (Redwood): Good point — Redwood's private deployments preserve KMS flows and we will not change the encryption context during a model variant fallback. We'll also attach the SOC2 appendix and the audit log schema.

[05:45] Sofia (Cascade): Ok great. For immediate mitigation — what can we do in the next 48 hours?

[05:52] Ethan (Redwood SE): Short list: 1) Run a KV prefill/warmup job that targets the high fan-out prefixes, 2) apply a temporary pre-burst capacity window, 3) deploy a consistent fallback policy to the most critical route groups. All of these are low-risk config changes.

[06:14] Ravi (Cascade): Who owns the warmup? Our SRE or Redwood?

[06:20] Maya (Redwood): We recommend your SRE own the actual prefill script since you control the job schedule, but Redwood can provide the warmup tool, small script examples, and a validation harness. We can pair with Sofia to get it running.

[06:34] Sofia (Cascade): We'll take ownership of the run — I'll run it in staging tonight and post results.

[06:42] Tom (Cascade): For the fallback policy, I'd like to see the simulation before we flip it in prod.

[06:48] Ethan (Redwood SE): Understood. I'll run the sim on a snapshot of the trace and return expected latencies and cost.

[07:00] Maya (Redwood): Good. Let's talk about runbook changes quickly — we saw confusion on which on-call should escalate to Redwood. We want a clear handoff.

[07:12] Lena (Redwood): We'll update the runbook to include explicit threshold triggers for Redwood escalation, a playbook for partial traffic cutover, and a template for post-incident notes. We'll also attach the Slack escalation channel and the PagerDuty routing we recommend.

[07:35] Ravi (Cascade): Any thoughts on longtail errors vs burst spikes? Our product team mutters about retry storms when clients get 429s.

[07:44] Ethan (Redwood SE): Retry storms amplify the problem. Two levers: client-side jittered backoff and server-side sticky tokens that indicate degraded mode to avoid retry amplification. We can provide SDK snippets for exponential jitter and a header that returns degrade-mode hints so SDKs can back off more gracefully.

[08:05] Tom (Cascade): Could the SDK change be a blocker for our mobile clients? It might require releases.

[08:12] Maya (Redwood): No blocker; SDK change will be incremental. We can expose the degrade hint in the response header and fallback to a 503 with Retry-After for mobile if needed. But we don't want to rely on client releases for the immediate fix.

[08:29] Sofia (Cascade): For monitoring, we saw some gaps: the synthetic probes don't cover the specific route permutations that the ETL touches.

[08:38] Ethan (Redwood SE): We can generate a synthetic probe template that hits the exact prefix set. Also add a KV-miss rate alert and a queued-requests alert. We'll supply PromQL and example thresholds.

[08:50] Ravi (Cascade): Awesome. One more ask on the legal/compliance side: can Redwood provide an immutable snapshot of the logs for audit?

[08:58] Lena (Redwood): We can provide exportable, signed log bundles for the incident window and integrate with your SIEM. We'll include guidance on retention.

[09:12] Tom (Cascade): I know ModelServeCo had an incident like this where they defaulted to a smaller model automatically and it changed outputs — our product team is worried about output regressions. How does Redwood guard against silently degrading quality?

[09:26] Ethan (Redwood SE): We have an eval set and prompts you can run against both the primary and fallback variants to check delta in outputs; Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles that preserve quality. We'll include a short eval harness in the follow-up bundle.

[09:46] Maya (Redwood): OK, next let's align on dates. Sofia will run warmup in staging by 2026-05-19, share results by 2026-05-22. Ethan will run simulation and provide histograms by 2026-05-25. Maya will share incident bundle by 2026-05-20. We should schedule the canary planning on 2026-05-27 — 30-minute slot.

[10:10] Ravi (Cascade): Sounds reasonable. Anything else on the long-tail reliability work?

[10:16] Ethan (Redwood SE): Longer term: 1) integrate prefix-aware prefill into your nightly pipeline, 2) add model-variant-specific telemetry, 3) create a canary gate that runs on a small percent of traffic with automated rollback if quality metrics drop.

[10:36] Tom (Cascade): For the canary gate, what metrics do you recommend we watch?

[10:42] Ethan (Redwood SE): p95 latency, token cost delta, and a simple quality check like perplexity on a shared prompt set; plus error rate and queued-requests. We'll pre-populate a suggested metric dashboard.

[10:57] Sofia (Cascade): On the prefilling script — is there a risk of double-writing or interfering with ETL?

[11:04] Ethan (Redwood SE): The recommended approach is read-only prefill that loads keys into KV without changing ETL artifacts. We'll provide idempotent scripts and a dry-run mode.

[11:20] Maya (Redwood): Quick housekeeping — we'll attach the SOC2 extract and audit log schema to the follow-up doc and mark the runbook diffs. Also, we'll propose a short pilot that uses a small pre-burst capacity for two weeks to validate cost vs reliability.

[11:40] Ravi (Cascade): If pilot cost looks reasonable, we can accept the buffer. If not, we'll explore more targeted warming + stricter prefill.

[11:50] Tom (Cascade): Anything else on legal or procurement? We might need an amendment if we change committed capacity for the pilot.

[12:00] Maya (Redwood): Procurement note noted — we'll loop in your procurement and our sales ops if the pilot requires a contract adjustment.

[12:10] Lena (Redwood): Final question — do you want Redwood to run the canary or you? We can offer to run the first canary to reduce friction.

[12:22] Ravi (Cascade): We would appreciate Redwood running the first one, at least until we have confidence.

[12:28] Maya (Redwood): Great — we'll plan to run the first pilot canary and provide a runbook for you to take over.

[12:36] Tom (Cascade): ok thanks, that helps.

[12:40] Maya (Redwood): Thanks everyone — recap of owners will be in the follow-up email. We'll close with the explicit next steps and action items. Any last questions?

[12:55] Sofia (Cascade): None from me, thanks.

[13:00] Ravi (Cascade): Thanks all.

[13:05] Maya (Redwood): End call.

Notes on transcription: There are occasional speaker overlaps and stutters. Some terms like 'KV' were transcribed as 'K V' in downstream exports, and 'quantized' sometimes shown as 'quantization parameter'.
additional_notes: References: incident bundle (redwood.in/incident/CH-472), warmup script examples in repo (link in follow-up), fallback-policy-template.yaml (attached after call).
